Notes for 2-12

Highlights

  • The Stan model is sensitive to the prior proportion of nulls (\(\pi_0\))
  • The Stan model with Poisson response has a very poor fit
    • Offsetting biased estimates of several parameters
  • The ‘Ribodiff’ model allows different dispersions for RNA and RPF samples in riboseq

\(\pi_0 = 0.8\)

I found an error - I was setting \(\pi_0 = 0.2\) (\(\pi_0\) is the prior proportion of null genes). The true proportion of null genes is \(0.8\). Setting \(\pi_0 = 0.8\) instead of to an incorrect value improves the performance of the stan models.

Poisson Stan fit

The sample normfactors plot isn’t great because of the big difference in y-axis scale, but the Poisson response model is completely missing (overestimating by a large margin) the true value, where the NB response model’s posterior is centered right at the true value.

Ribodiff

  • We saw quite poor performance from this method in the ribovi paper (and I think also in one of Ran’s papers?)
  • Their model does allow different dispersions for RNA and RPF samples
  • Their model does not have any pairing between RNA and RPF from the same biological sample

Simulation description

I replicated a simple simulation setting from BYN PLOSOne 2020 and compared the performance of edgeR and my Stan models on this data set. The setting is just a two-group comparison, with baseline means and dispersions sampled from edgeR estimates produced by a large real data set and FC simulated from 1.5 + exp(1). There are no random effects.

  • Stan model with negative binomial response and estimated dispersion is ok
    • Better logFC estimates than edgeR
    • Similar ROC to edgeR
    • Liberal FDR control, where edgeR is conservative
    • Overestimates (truly) large dispersions, where edgeR underestimates
  • Stan model with Poisson response is quite poor
